evidence.description: cargo test --workspace: 146 passed, 0 failed. New certification: docs/conformance/diagnostics/15_sem_contract_violation.aipo and 16_sem_return_contract.aipo (a provable mismatch is AIPO_SEM_CONTRACT_VIOLATION_STATIC before execution, while 12/13 keep the unprovable ones as runtime contract faults), docs/conformance/programs/16_interface_contracts.aipo and diagnostics/17_runtime_interface_contract.aipo and 18_runtime_interface_arity.aipo (structural conformance for an interface contract, checked by caller-visible arity and naming the struct in the fault), docs/conformance/programs/17_unicode_nfc.aipo (NFC at the literal, concatenation, interpolation, join, replace, format, case mapping and reverse boundaries), docs/conformance/programs/18_tolerant_slices_and_clamp.aipo and diagnostics/19_runtime_clamp_inverted_bounds.aipo (tolerant slices for List/String/Bytes, recoverable inverted clamp bounds). At the unit level: test_string_literals_are_nfc_normalized in crates/aipo-lexer/src/lib.rs, test_string_operations_preserve_nfc in crates/aipo-stdlib/tests/stdlib_tests.rs, and test_string_concatenation_preserves_nfc, test_interface_contract_accepts_a_conforming_operation and test_interface_contract_names_the_failing_struct in crates/aipo-vm/tests/data_and_errors.rs

cargo fmt --all -- --check (exit 0), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings (zero warnings), cargo test --workspace (146 passed, 0 failed) and cargo doc --workspace --no-deps (no warnings) are all green; prumo validate, prumo doctor and prumo docs verify/authority/contradictions/audit are clean; full output in docs/evidence/P00-G15-static-contracts-and-interface-conformance.md

Decisions taken from canon instead of invented: a provable contract mismatch is reported before execution while an unprovable one stays a contract fault at the boundary (Language Reference section 4); an interface is structural, so using it as a contract asks whether the value exposes the declared operations (Sintaxe Canonica, Interfaces e satisfy); inverted clamp bounds are a value outside a valid range and therefore a recoverable Failure, unlike an index outside a range, which is a fault (Language Reference section 4 vs 16); slices are tolerant/clamped while exact indices fault (Aipo Language - Especificacao Viva, List model); NFC belongs to the String construction boundaries. All recorded in docs/adp/ADP-001-byte-and-core-types-as-values.md (now resolved: Q1/Q2 by P00-G10, Q3/Q4/Q5 here) and in docs/adp/ADP-002-construction-hooks-and-runtime-contracts.md, which also records the interface arity defect this goal found and corrected and the residual limits (name+arity is not a full signature check; normalizing the constant pool is deliberately out of scope) instead of hiding them
